title: First-run guided experience: hero walkthrough and screenshot assets for Optimize toolkit
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Design a compact, first-run guided experience and a set of launch-ready visual assets (hero frames, step walkthroughs, inline screenshots) that teach users how the Optimize toolkit recommends batching, KV caching, and quantization presets. This ticket covers content/visuals for the in-app first-run tour and the static assets used in docs/release notes.

Scope:
- 3 hero frames for the first-run modal (Welcome + key value props + quick action CTA).
- 4 walkthrough steps: workload detection, batching suggestion, KV cache explanation, quant preset chooser. Each step needs a high-fidelity screenshot + callout overlay.
- Visual variants for Desktop (1200px), Tablet (900px), and Mobile (390px).
- Annotated handoff sheet for engineering with copy, alt text, spacing/token notes, and accessibility contrast checks.
- Lightweight motion spec for the in-modal transitions (fade/slide) and microcopy for the CTA flows.

Constraints/Design decisions:
- Keep modal width <= 920px to avoid expensive reflows on low-end devices.
- Use simplified quant presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with a short tooltip describing latency/cost/quality tradeoffs. Avoid jargon (no mention of bit quantization levels in modal).
- Batching recommendation cards must display estimated token cost delta and expected tail latency (p90) impact as a single-line summary to keep cognitive load low.
- Avoid showing raw telemetry in onboarding; show aggregated example metrics only. Engineering must wire live numbers later (ENG-2110).

Deliverables:
- Figma file: first-run flow + exportable slices for engineering.
- PNG and SVG exports for docs (hero, step thumbnails, icons).
- Annotated handoff (CSV-like checklist in Figma + single Confluence page link).
- Copy deck with microcopy variants (2x A/B).
- Acceptance criteria checklist for design review and PM signoff.
